canada.title: 'No merit' to U.S. claims Canada is interfering ahead of midterms: Carney
canada.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney says there is “no merit” to American claims that Canadians might be interfering in U.S. politics ahead of November’s midterm elections.

canada.title: Eadie faces crowded field — including former councillor — in bid for fifth term in Mynarski
canada.summary: THE city’s most crowded council race has a little bit of everything: a long-serving incumbent, a former ward councillor in the 1980s, an unsuccessful candidate in the last municipal election seeking a rematch and three political newcomers.

canada.title: Canadian woman dies in U.S. after fears of detainment prevented her from seeking medical care
canada.summary: Last month Paige Adamson was stopped at a U.S.-Canada border crossing and interrogated for hours about whether she had unlawfully voted in a U.S. election. She died at home on Sunday after a fall, telling friends she was scared of being detained if she sought medical care.

canada.title: As the Yukon moves to lift rent control, we asked how many MLAs are landlords
canada.summary: With rent control and no-fault evictions on the table in the Yukon legislature, CBC News asked members of the legislative assembly whether or not they’re landlords.

canada.title: Workshop in Haines Junction teaches fish canning and connects generations
canada.summary: A fish-canning workshop in Haines Junction, Yukon, helps residents preserve food while also passing knowledge between generations. Participants say the skills can help reduce food waste, save money and keep cultural traditions alive.

canada.title: Military could begin Arctic sensor installations next summer
canada.summary: National Defence plans to install 47 sensor stations across the North starting as early as next summer to bolster Norad’s surveillance and early warning abilities, according to recently published regulatory filings.

canada.title: European leaders join Hungary’s 1956 revolution commemoration as Magyar resets EU ties
canada.summary: BUDAPEST, Hungary (AP) — Numerous foreign guests representing countries across Europe visited Hungary’s capital on Friday to take part in an event commemorating the 70th anniversary of Hungary’s 1956 anti-Soviet uprising — and to signal a new chapter in their countries’ relations with Budapest after the ouster of former Prime Minister Viktor Orbán.
